run.title: Product Research
assumptions: Product costs are estimates: supplier prices are starting prices before shipping
Ad counts only include ads that use the exact product words, so real numbers can be higher
Green on a map means we found nobody else selling this exact item there, not that nobody does
Lash adhesive is a cosmetic used near the eye: selling in the EU or UK needs a safety assessment and product registration

headline: No product is ready to test today. The under-eye CC cream has the strongest proof: one Italian shop has advertised it alone for over six months. But it copies Tarte's best-seller and needs EU cosmetics paperwork first.

products.name: Under-Eye CC Cream Compact (DermoCosmetic)
products.store_products: 2 products: this compact and a brush
products.one_liner: One Italian shop has advertised this alone for six months, which is strong proof. But it copies Tarte's best-seller, which Sephora and Ulta sell, and look-alikes cost £6 on Amazon UK.
why: DermoCosmetic runs all 61 Italian ads for "correttore occhiaie" and its oldest has run since 30 March
It is a look-alike of Tarte's Colored Clay CC Undereye Corrector, sold by Sephora, Ulta, Kohl's and Macy's at US$32
Look-alikes are easy to find: £5.99 on Amazon UK and on Temu in Australia
products.risk: Copying a famous brand's look invites ad takedowns, and EU cosmetics need a safety report and registration before the first sale.
next: Get a quote for an EU cosmetic safety report and registration from a Responsible Person service
If it is affordable, test a market DermoCosmetic is not in (Spain or Portugal) with your own branding
products.best_region: None of the six. The proof is in Italy, which these checks do not cover; Spain or Portugal would copy that playbook.

snapshot.icp: Women 35-60 with dark circles or mature under-eye skin who want quick coverage
snapshot.job: Hide dark circles in 30 seconds without creasing
snapshot.cogs: About €2-4 landed for a generic compact (estimate: look-alikes retail at £6)
snapshot.claims: High coverage, does not crease after 8 hours, 3 shades, built-in mirror
snapshot.demoable: Yes: before and after under one eye is instant and visual

gates.name: Chain gate
gates.why: Ulta, Sephora and Kohl's sell Tarte's original in the US; Walmart Canada lists a look-alike at CA$18

gates.name: Copies gate
gates.why: Look-alikes from £5.99 on Amazon UK and on Temu; Italy and Spain were not checked

gates.name: Swarm gate
gates.why: One brand owns the Italian ads

gates.name: Bulk gate
gates.why: Small and light

gates.name: Regulated gate
gates.why: A cosmetic: the EU needs a Responsible Person, a safety report and registration before selling

angles: Spanish or Portuguese version of the same before-and-after ads
Men's under-eye concealer: tired eyes after work
New mums: hide sleepless nights in 30 seconds
Glasses wearers: coverage that does not crease under frames
TAKEN: "Does not crease, even after 8 hours" for mature skin (DermoCosmetic's main message)

compare.note: The same rose-gold square compact with a mirror: Tarte's original, and many look-alikes.

products.advertiser_takeaway: In Italy DermoCosmetic is alone: all 61 ads for "correttore occhiaie" are theirs, the oldest from 30 March, and 23 started this month. Six months of spend means it pays. The ads are Italian, so this proves Italy, not the six countries on the map.

category_notes.us: Sephora and Ulta sell many CC creams; the exact compact is Tarte's original.
category_notes.de: dm and Douglas sell other CC creams (tubes and sticks), not this compact. The photo search returned no results in Germany.

products.name: Magnetic Tennis Swing Trainer (SwngPro)
products.one_liner: Only one brand advertises it and the margin is huge, but identical copies already sit in Amazon's top results in every country, from about US$30. Worth watching, not testing yet.
why: Swng runs 60+ ads and is ramping fast (36 started in October), with almost no other advertisers
A supplier sells it from about US$8, so roughly 90% of the US$89 price is left for ads and profit
But copies are easy to find: Amazon US result 3 at US$29.99, UK result 2 at £17, Germany result 1 at €45.99
products.risk: Swng's ads are only six weeks old, so they are not yet proof it pays, and Amazon copies undercut US$89 by two thirds.
next: Check again in early December: if Swng's late-August ads are still running, the ads pay
Then test it for padel or pickleball players, which Swng ignores: 3 short ads, about €20 a day for 5 days
products.best_region: None yet. Every country has a cheaper copy in Amazon's top results, and Walmart Canada lists one at CA$23.

snapshot.icp: Recreational tennis players, 25-55, who want to improve without paying for lessons
snapshot.job: Groove a consistent swing at home, with instant feedback
snapshot.cogs: About US$8 before shipping; roughly US$12-15 landed (estimate)
snapshot.claims: Audible snap when the swing is right; 5 resistance levels (11-33 N); 15-day drill program
snapshot.demoable: Yes: the snap sound on a good swing is made for short video

gates.name: Chain gate
gates.why: Walmart Canada lists the same stick at CA$23 (it may be a marketplace seller). No chain found elsewhere

gates.name: Copies gate
gates.why: Cheaper copies sit in Amazon's top 5 in every country, from £17 in the UK and €13 in Germany

gates.name: Swarm gate
gates.why: One brand runs the ads; only one other page, which also sells SwngPro

gates.name: Bulk gate
gates.why: Small and light

gates.name: Regulated gate
gates.why: No health claims needed

angles: Padel players: the fastest-growing racket sport in Europe
Pickleball players in the US
Junior players: parents buying practice between lessons
Coaches and clubs: a set for group drills
TAKEN: "Win the match without lessons" (Swng's main message)

compare.note: The same chrome tube with a white grip and snap mechanism; Amazon sells the same design in other colours.

products.advertiser_takeaway: Swng is almost alone: 60+ ads, ramping fast since late August, and the only other page also sells SwngPro. That is the pattern to like, but it is only six weeks old, so it is not yet proof the ads pay.

category_notes.au: The chain listings are other tennis trainers (rebound balls, reflex sticks), not this stick.
category_notes.us: DICK'S sells other tennis trainers, not this stick; the copies are on Amazon.
category_notes.uk: Decathlon sells other tennis trainers, not this stick; the copy is on Amazon UK.
category_notes.de: Decathlon sells other tennis trainers, not this stick; the copies are on Amazon Germany.
category_notes.nz: Rebel Sport sells other tennis trainers, not this stick.

Advertisers.head: 1 brand, 60+ ads
Advertisers.detail: Swng runs all 60+ ads that name SwngPro, rising fast since late August. The only other page also sells SwngPro.

products.name: Pre-Glued Lash Starter Kit (Lola's Lashes)
products.store_products: 250 products, all lashes and lash care
products.one_liner: Nobody else sells this exact kit, so the map is green. But the category is full: big brands in every chain, 28+ advertisers and Amazon kits with thousands of reviews.
why: Ardell, KISS imPRESS and GLAM pre-glued clusters sit in Target, Walmart, Kmart, Priceline and Chemist Warehouse from about US$12
At least 28 brands advertise "pre-glued lashes"; Lola's alone runs 147 of 250 ads and has advertised since February
Amazon is heavy: 10,550+ bought last month in the US, and the top listing in Canada has 25,100 reviews
products.risk: You would need your own lash brand, safety paperwork and creative good enough to beat established beauty brands on cost per sale.
next: Skip this as a product test. If beauty appeals, look for a lash-care add-on (remover, storage, aftercare) with fewer advertisers
products.best_region: None. The map is green only because no one copies Lola's design; rival pre-glued kits are in big chains in all six countries.

snapshot.icp: Women 18-40 who want salon-style lash extensions without salon cost or infill appointments
snapshot.job: Fuller lashes at home that last several days
snapshot.cogs: Roughly £3-6 landed for a generic pre-glued kit (estimate, not checked)
snapshot.claims: 5-10 day hold, waterproof, patented stick-and-clamp applicator, vegan; Beauty Awards 2025 shortlist
snapshot.demoable: Yes: before and after, three-step application on camera

gates.name: Chain gate
gates.why: No chain sells a copy of this exact kit, but Superdrug and Boots stock Lola's own kit, and every chain sells rival pre-glued clusters

gates.name: Copies gate
gates.why: No other seller copies this exact design. The rival kits look clearly different, so this gate passes, but the category is full

gates.name: Swarm gate
gates.why: Crowded, not a swarm: 12 of 28 brands are new in the last two months, and the biggest shops are all over a year old

gates.name: Bulk gate
gates.why: Small and light

gates.name: Regulated gate
gates.why: A cosmetic with adhesive used near the eye: needs EU/UK cosmetic safety assessment and registration before selling

angles: Lashes for glasses wearers: lengths that don't touch the lenses
Gym and swim lashes: sweat-proof for workouts
Mature eyes: soft, light clusters for sparse lashes over 45
Bride and bridesmaid kit: one box for the whole party
TAKEN: "No more infills" salon-cost saving (Lola's main message)

compare.match_name: Lola's Lashes kit on Amazon UK (£20)
compare.note: Every exact match was Lola's own kit, sold by the brand or its stockists, including Lola's on Amazon UK at £20. No other seller makes this design.

products.advertiser_takeaway: Lola's Lashes leads: 147 of the first 250 ads are theirs, running since February. Behind them are established names (Unicorn Cosmetics, Tatti Lashes, imPRESS) with shops over a year old. It works, but it is a fight between real brands, not an open gap.

category_notes.au: The chain listings are rival brands (Ardell, GLAM by Manicare), not this kit.
category_notes.us: Target and Walmart sell rival brands (Ardell, KISS imPRESS), not this kit.
category_notes.uk: Superdrug and Boots sell Lola's own kit and rival brands.
category_notes.ca: Walmart and Shoppers Drug Mart sell rival brands (Ardell, QUO, KISS), not this kit.
category_notes.de: Douglas and Boozyshop sell rival kits; Boozyshop also sells Lola's own kit.
category_notes.nz: Chemist Warehouse sells GLAM by Manicare clusters, not this kit.

Same.head: Only the brand itself
Same.detail: Every exact match is Lola's own kit, sold by the brand or its stockists (Superdrug, Boozyshop, Amazon). Rival kits look different but are everywhere.

products.name: Neck Firming Cream (Mudganics)
products.store_products: 42 products, Australian skincare, also sold wholesale
products.one_liner: The map is green only because this is Mudganics' own formula. Neck creams are a swarm: 40 advertisers, 38 new in two months, and 431,000+ bought on Amazon US last month.
why: 40 brands advertise "neck firming cream" and 38 of them started in the last two months: a swarm
Amazon is enormous: 431,550+ bought last month in the US, top listings with 19,000-37,900 reviews
You cannot buy this formula: you would need your own private-label cream against StriVectin, Olay and dozens of Amazon brands
products.risk: Firming and anti-ageing claims on a cosmetic need evidence and safety paperwork, and Meta reviews before-and-after ads strictly.
next: Skip it. Demand is real, but sellers are flooding in faster than it grows
products.best_region: None. Chains such as Kmart, Walmart, John Lewis and Douglas sell neck creams in every country checked.

snapshot.icp: Women 45-65 bothered by a crepey or sagging neck
snapshot.job: Firm and smooth the neck and chest skin that face creams skip
snapshot.cogs: About A$6-12 for a private-label cream with packaging (estimate)
snapshot.claims: Sea buckthorn and peptides; 67% saw visible results in a 4-week trial
snapshot.demoable: Yes: neck before and after, but it takes weeks to show

gates.name: Chain gate
gates.why: No chain sells this exact cream; chains sell many other neck creams

gates.name: Copies gate
gates.why: Nobody copies Mudganics' formula, but the category is full

gates.name: Swarm gate
gates.why: 40 brands advertise, 38 of them new in the last two months

gates.name: Bulk gate
gates.why: Small and light

gates.name: Regulated gate
gates.why: A cosmetic with firming claims: needs safety paperwork and proof for the claims

angles: Men's neck and jawline cream
"Tech neck" for under-40s who look down at phones all day
Post-weight-loss loose skin
Neck cream plus gua sha tool bundle
TAKEN: "Don't stop your skincare at your jawline" (Mudganics' main message)

compare.match_name: Skin Physics neck cream at Priceline (A$80), a different brand
compare.note: Every match was another brand's neck cream. Mudganics' formula is sold only by Mudganics.

products.advertiser_takeaway: This is a swarm: 40 brands, 38 of them with ads started in the last two months, including several brand-new shop names. Mudganics itself only started advertising on 28 September. Lots of people are piling in, and nobody has proven staying power yet.

Same.head: Own formula
Same.detail: Nobody else sells Mudganics' cream. The real competition is hundreds of other neck creams.

category_notes.de: The photo search returned no results in Germany; Douglas and Amazon Germany sell many neck creams.

products.name: No-Rinse Foam Paw Cleanser (Dandylion)
products.one_liner: Dandylion is an established brand already in Target, Chewy and Petco, and the same foam-and-brush bottle sells from about US$6 under dozens of names. Too cheap and too crowded for a newcomer.
why: The same foam-and-brush bottle is in the top results everywhere: Amazon US result 2 at US$13.95 with 1,100 reviews
38 brands advertise "paw cleaner" and 32 of them started in the last two months: a swarm
At about CA$20 a bottle, there is little room to pay for ads against Wet Ones, Bugalugs and Pets at Home's own range
products.risk: A low-priced liquid: shipping and ad costs eat most of the margin unless customers reorder.
next: Skip it. If pet care appeals, look for a higher-priced pet product with fewer sellers
products.best_region: None. Every country checked has cheap look-alikes with hundreds or thousands of reviews.

snapshot.icp: Dog owners, often in cities or rainy climates, who walk their dog daily
snapshot.job: Clean muddy paws after a walk without a bath
snapshot.cogs: About US$2-4 for a generic foam bottle with brush head (estimate)
snapshot.margin: About 70-80% at CA$20 before shipping a liquid (estimate)
snapshot.demoable: Yes: muddy paw before, clean paw after

gates.name: Chain gate
gates.why: Target, BIG W and Pets at Home sell foam paw cleaners; Dandylion's own bottle is in Target and Petco

gates.name: Copies gate
gates.why: Cheaper look-alikes are in the top results in every country, many with 1,000+ reviews

gates.name: Swarm gate
gates.why: 38 brands advertise "paw cleaner", 32 new in the last two months (the phrase also covers paw-washing cups)

gates.name: Bulk gate
gates.why: Small, but a liquid

gates.name: Regulated gate
gates.why: A pet grooming product; avoid medical claims

angles: Winter salt and grit: protect paws in snowy cities
Allergy season: wash pollen off paws
Subscription refill for daily walkers
Cat litter-paw cleanup
TAKEN: "Vet-dermatologist approved, lick-safe" (Dandylion's main message)

compare.note: Photo matches were Dandylion's own bottle at its stockists; look-alikes from other brands use the same foam-and-brush bottle.

products.advertiser_takeaway: It's a swarm: 38 brands, 32 of them new in the last two months, several from shops opened this year. The phrase also catches paw-washing cups, but the pattern is clear: many sellers piling in, and Dandylion is not among the top advertisers.

country_takeaways.us: Google's page for these words is off-topic in the US (student pages and unrelated sites); rely on the product strip and Amazon.

category_notes.ca: The photo search returned no results in Canada; Dandylion is Canadian and sold at Pet Valu.
